title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: policy insights columns withdrawn from the roadmap
summary: The withdrawal notice, roadmap fields, documented counters and role-management instructions are supported. The access guidance needs correction: role-group membership alone does not grant access to policy alerts, and administrative-unit scoping also limits which policies members can see.

claims.quote: This item is no longer accurate and is being removed from the roadmap.  We apologize for the inconvenience.

claims.claim: The item planned two policy-performance columns on the Communication Compliance home page.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: The second planned column reported parent items meeting policy conditions.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: No source states that this withdrawn item changes the existing pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance "policy insights" "parent" default columns. Opened Investigate and remediate Communication Compliance alerts and Get started with Communication Compliance; read the roadmap withdrawal notice. No replacement of existing pages is stated.

claims.claim: Learn does not document the planned real-time parent-item columns as of this check.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance "policy insights" "parent" default columns; Communication Compliance policy insights columns licensing price meter 172016. Read the Policies page section of Investigate and remediate Communication Compliance alerts; it documents daily counters, not these columns.

claims.claim: The Policies page lists per-policy Messages scanned today counts for the current day's in-scope users and locations.
claims.quote: Messages scanned today: The total number of messages that the policy scanned on the current day for users and locations that are in scope of the policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says a zero or low scan count may indicate an overly strict policy, such as a single-user or unused-location scope.
claims.quote: If the value in the column is 0 or a low number, it might be because the policy is too strict. For example, the policy might be focused on just one user or on just one location that the in-scope user doesn't use.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Roles and role groups control access to the Communication Compliance solution and its Policies page.
claims.quote: To use any of the Communication Compliance-related tools in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need the appropriate permissions. The easiest way to assign roles is to add the user to the appropriate role group

claims.claim: The permissions page lists the six stated roles and role groups as making Communication Compliance available as a menu option.
claims.quote: To make Communication Compliance available as a menu option in Microsoft Purview portal and to continue with these configuration steps, you must be assigned to one of the following roles or role groups:
claims.fix: Keep the attributed list, but add: "The Learn overview separately says that, by default, Global Administrators don't have access to Communication Compliance features." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance#workflow, whose excerpt states that qualification; the two Learn pages disagree.

claims.claim: Administrative-unit scoping restricts the policies a role-group member can view and manage on the Policies page.
claims.quote: If your role group is scoped by one or more admin units, you see a message at the top of the page that you can only view and manage the policies that you're scoped for.

claims.claim: Role-group membership is managed in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Role groups in the left navigation pane. ... Select the Communication Compliance role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the specified role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference lists Identity and Member as applicable to Security & Compliance.
claims.quote: Applicable: Exchange Server 2010, Exchange Server 2013, Exchange Server 2016, Exchange Server 2019, Exchange Server SE, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance, Built-in security add-on for on-premises mailboxes

claims.claim: Role-group permission changes can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After configuring your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: The Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote: | Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes | No | No | No |

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Role-group membership decides who can open policy alerts, and Analysts and Investigators can access and investigate alerts without a stated further condition.
claims.quote:
To view and act on alerts, assign users the following permissions:
- The Communication Compliance Analysts or the Communication Compliance Investigators role group
- Reviewer in the policy that is associated with the alert
claims.fix: Replace the At rollout bullet with "Check membership of the Communication Compliance role groups to review solution access." Replace the alert-access clause in Governance controls with "To view and act on alerts, the investigation page requires the Communication Compliance Analysts or Communication Compliance Investigators role group and reviewer assignment in the policy associated with the alert." The source is https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-investigate-remediate.

claims.claim: Membership of the Communication Compliance role groups is the only control that bears on the displayed counts.
claims.quote: If your role group is scoped by one or more admin units, you see a message at the top of the page that you can only view and manage the policies that you're scoped for.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence "Membership of the Communication Compliance role groups is the only control that bears on this item, because the counts appear on a page inside the solution." The existing paragraph already describes administrative-unit scoping, which also restricts policy visibility.

claims.claim: Communication Compliance requires a supported subscription and appropriate licences assigned to users.
claims.quote: To access and use Communication Compliance, administrators need to verify that their organization has a supported subscription and that users have the appropriate licenses assigned.
